Yes. The closest match is decoupled split learning with an auxiliary loss: instead of propagating error signals back across the client-server split, the client uses a local auxiliary classifier for its own error signal while the server trains on transmitted activations with the true loss. This removes the need to send backward gradients, cutting split-learning communication roughly in half while maintaining performance comparable to standard split learning [1].

Related papers also avoid standard backprop-style credit assignment, but with different goals. Predictive coding with highway error propagation and Error Diffusion both replace backpropagation with alternative error-routing mechanisms for training deep or biologically constrained networks, rather than focusing on reducing data exchange in shared distributed architectures [5,7]. Other communication-efficient work here mainly compresses gradients, weight updates, or critic parameters instead of avoiding error-signal propagation altogether [2,4,10].
